BlackRock and Ondo Launch Tokenized ETF Portfolio Strategies for Non-U.S. Investors According to WSJ, BlackRock and Ondo Finance have launched Ondo Intelligent Portfolios, bringing BlackRock’s customized ETF portfolio strategies onchain as transferable tokens for the first time. Available to eligible investors outside the U.S., the initial lineup includes three strategies: High Income (BLKHIon), Diversified Growth (BLKDIGon) and High Growth (BLKGRWon). Investors can access ETF portfolio exposure through a single transferable token using major wallets and DeFi applications. — link

Highlight Clip: Coinbase CEO: Every Early User Got a Whole Bitcoin to Try the App Coinbase CEO: Every Early User Got a Whole Bitcoin to Try the App In an interview published by The Wolf Of All Streets on September 20, 2026, Coinbase co-founder and CEO Brian Armstrong said that when the Coinbase app launched in 2012, he gave one bitcoin to every person willing to try it, when each bitcoin was worth about $5 to $10. Around 1,000 people received the giveaway, and years later, some returned to tell him the bitcoin was worth $60,000 to $100,000. Armstrong also recalled that few people took crypto seriously in its early days, while the U.S. government now holds a strategic Bitcoin reserve — something he said he could hardly have imagined at the time. — link

SEC Commissioner Peirce Calls for Zero-Knowledge Proofs to Replace Data-Heavy KYC/AML Practices SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce said the agency’s Innovation Exemption provides a temporary pathway for tokenized securities to trade through AMMs, helping prevent overseas markets from monopolizing tokenized exposure to U.S. equities while serving as a bridge to longer-term rules. She also criticized the current KYC/AML model for creating ever-larger “data haystacks” with limited effectiveness while turning the financial system into a “panopticon,” and called for zero-knowledge proofs and attribute-based credentials to verify compliance without collecting or repeatedly storing users’ sensitive personal data. — link

New York Sues Prediction Market Platform Polymarket Over Alleged Illegal Gambling Operations According to Reuters, the State of New York filed a lawsuit on Thursday against decentralized prediction market operator Polymarket, accusing the platform of conducting an illegal gambling operation. The legal action follows related enforcement measures by New York Attorney General Letitia James targeting prediction platforms—including earlier actions against Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini—alleging the unlicensed offering of event-based betting within the state. — link
